rows.stem: If ‘n’ is a natural number, then which of the following numbers end with zero ?
rows.solution:
A number ends with zero only if it is divisible by 10, that is, only if its prime factorisation contains both 2 and 5.

\((3 \times 2)^n = 2^n \times 3^n\) and \((6 \times 2)^n = 2^{2n} \times 3^n\) have no factor 5, and \((5 \times 3)^n = 3^n \times 5^n\) has no factor 2. Only \((2 \times 5)^n = 10^n\) contains both, and it ends with zero for every natural number n.

This is option (B) \((2 \times 5)^n\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: In a lottery, there are 5 prizes and 20 blanks. The probability of getting a prize is :
rows.solution:
There are \(5 + 20 = 25\) tickets in all, of which 5 carry a prize.

\(P(\text{prize}) = \dfrac{5}{25} = \dfrac{1}{5}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{1}{5}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: If \(2x + 3y = 15\) and \(3x + 2y = 25\), then the value of \(x - y\) is :
rows.solution:
Subtract the first equation from the second:

\((3x + 2y) - (2x + 3y) = 25 - 15\), so \(x - y = 10\).

(Solving fully gives \(x = 9\), \(y = -1\).) This is option (C) \(10\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\angle A = \angle C\), AB = 6 cm, AP = 12 cm, CP = 4 cm. Then length of CD is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that AC and BD are straight lines crossing at P (A-P-C and B-P-D), forming triangles APB and CPD with the equal angles marked at A and C, is shown only in the drawing; the stem never places P or D. The drawing also shows AB vertical over E and the rectangle-like outline BDCE. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
In the figure AC and BD are straight lines that cross at P. In triangles APB and CPD:

\(\angle A = \angle C\) (given) and \(\angle APB = \angle CPD\) (vertically opposite angles).

So \(\Delta APB \sim \Delta CPD\) (AA similarity), and \(\dfrac{AB}{CD} = \dfrac{AP}{CP}\).

\(\dfrac{6}{CD} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3\), so \(CD = 2\) cm, which is option (A) 2 cm.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: The sum of zeroes of the polynomial \(\sqrt{2}x^2 - 17\) are given as :
rows.solution:
\(\sqrt{2}x^2 - 17\) is \(ax^2 + bx + c\) with \(a = \sqrt{2}\), \(b = 0\) and \(c = -17\).

Sum of the zeroes \(= -\dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{0}{\sqrt{2}} = 0\). (The zeroes are \(\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{17}{\sqrt{2}}}\), equal and opposite.) This is option (C) \(0\).

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: If the area of the base of a cone is 51 \(\text{cm}^2\) and its volume is 85 \(\text{cm}^3\), then the vertical height of the cone is given as :
rows.solution:
Volume of a cone \(= \dfrac{1}{3} \times (\text{area of base}) \times h\).

\(85 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 51 \times h = 17h\), so \(h = 5\) cm, which is option (D) 5 cm.

rows.subtopic: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
rows.stem: Prove that \(6 - \sqrt{7}\) is irrational number, given that \(\sqrt{7}\) is an irrational number.
rows.solution:
Suppose, to the contrary, that \(6 - \sqrt{7}\) is rational. Then \(6 - \sqrt{7} = \dfrac{p}{q}\), where p and q are integers and \(q \neq 0\).

Rearranging, \(\sqrt{7} = 6 - \dfrac{p}{q} = \dfrac{6q - p}{q}\). Since p and q are integers, \(6q - p\) is an integer, so \(\dfrac{6q - p}{q}\) is rational. That makes \(\sqrt{7}\) rational, which contradicts the given fact that \(\sqrt{7}\) is irrational.

So the assumption is wrong, and \(6 - \sqrt{7}\) is irrational.

Write \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) in the first term:

\(\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} = \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\dfrac{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}} = \dfrac{\cos^3\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}\).

In the second term, \(\sin\theta - \cos\theta = -(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)\), so

LHS \(= \dfrac{\cos^3\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta} - \dfrac{\sin^3\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta} = \dfrac{\cos^3\theta - \sin^3\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}\).

Using \(a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)\):

\(= \dfrac{(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta + \sin\theta\cos\theta)}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta} = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta + \sin\theta\cos\theta\).

Since \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\), LHS \(= 1 + \sin\theta\cos\theta =\) RHS.

rows.stem:
A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of \(60^\circ\) at the centre. Find the area of the corresponding minor segment of the circle.

(Use \(\pi = 3{\cdot}14\) and \(\sqrt{3} = 1{\cdot}73\))
rows.solution:
Let O be the centre and AB the chord, so \(OA = OB = 14\) cm and \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\).

Area of the minor sector \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times \pi r^2 = \dfrac{3{\cdot}14 \times 14 \times 14}{6} = \dfrac{615{\cdot}44}{6} = 102{\cdot}57\) cm\(^2\) (to two decimal places).

Triangle AOB has \(OA = OB\) and \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\), so it is equilateral with side 14 cm.

Area of \(\Delta AOB = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 14^2 = \dfrac{1{\cdot}73}{4} \times 196 = 84{\cdot}77\) cm\(^2\).

Area of the minor segment \(=\) area of the sector \(-\) area of \(\Delta AOB = 102{\cdot}57 - 84{\cdot}77 = 17{\cdot}8\) cm\(^2\).

rows.stem:
The mode of the following frequency distribution is 55. Find the missing frequencies ‘a’ and ‘b’.

| Class Interval | 0 – 15 | 15 – 30 | 30 – 45 | 45 – 60 | 60 – 75 | 75 – 90 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 6 | 7 | a | 15 | 10 | b | 51 |
rows.solution:
The mode is 55, which lies in the class 45 to 60, so this is the modal class: \(l = 45\), \(h = 15\), \(f_1 = 15\), \(f_0 = a\) (the class before) and \(f_2 = 10\) (the class after).

Mode \(= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h\):

\(55 = 45 + \dfrac{15 - a}{30 - a - 10} \times 15\), so \(10 = \dfrac{15(15 - a)}{20 - a}\).

\(10(20 - a) = 15(15 - a)\), that is \(200 - 10a = 225 - 15a\), so \(5a = 25\) and \(a = 5\).

The frequencies total 51: \(6 + 7 + a + 15 + 10 + b = 51\), so \(a + b = 13\) and \(b = 13 - 5 = 8\).

\(a = 5\) and \(b = 8\). (Check: 15 is then the largest frequency, so 45 to 60 is indeed the modal class.)

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: Prerna saves ₹ 32 during the first month, ₹ 36 in the second month and ₹ 40 in the third month. If she continues to save in this manner, in how many months will she save ₹ 2,000 ?
rows.solution:
The monthly savings \(32, 36, 40, \ldots\) form an AP with \(a = 32\) and \(d = 4\). Let n be the number of months, so \(S_n = 2000\):

\(\dfrac{n}{2}[2 \times 32 + (n - 1) \times 4] = 2000\)

\(\dfrac{n}{2}(60 + 4n) = 2000\), so \(n(30 + 2n) = 2000\), that is \(2n^2 + 30n - 2000 = 0\), or \(n^2 + 15n - 1000 = 0\).

\(n^2 + 40n - 25n - 1000 = 0\), so \((n + 40)(n - 25) = 0\), and \(n = -40\) or \(n = 25\).

A number of months cannot be negative, so \(n = 25\).

(Check: \(S_{25} = \dfrac{25}{2}(64 + 96) = \dfrac{25}{2} \times 160 = 2000\).) Prerna will save ₹ 2,000 in 25 months.
